feature: Pinch direction picks what the timeline zooms
summary: A pinch on the timeline now zooms the way your fingers spread: side to side opens out time, up and down makes the rows taller, on the slant does both.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording so the timeline shows, on a Mac with a trackpad.

try.do: Put the pointer over the tracks and spread two fingers side to side.
Spread two fingers straight up and down over the tracks.
Squeeze two fingers together on a slant, thumb low left and finger high right.
Start a sideways pinch, then let your fingers drift up and down before lifting them.
Hold Option and pinch up and down, then hold Shift and pinch side to side.

evaluate: Does a sideways pinch change only the time scale, and an up and down pinch only the row height?
Does the pinch pick its direction quickly enough that you never notice the first moment of waiting?
Is 35 degrees either side the right width for 'straight', or do your natural pinches land on the slant and zoom both?
Does a pinch stay on the way it started even when your fingers drift?
rough: The walks drive made-up fingers through the same steering the trackpad feeds, so the axis choice is proven; that the trackpad's own touches reach the timeline on a real Mac could not be tried here, because nobody can pinch a trackpad from a script. If a pinch still zooms both ways whichever way you spread, the touches are not arriving.
The first few percent of a pinch are held back until the direction is known (about 2 mm of finger travel), then applied at once. You may feel that as a tiny delay at the start.
